newsitem.title: CHINA: China sets rules on monetary consulting body.
newsitem.headline: China sets rules on monetary consulting body.

text.p: China has issued detailed regulations governing the establishment of the People's Bank of China Monetary Policy Committee, officials and the state media said on Tuesday.

The establishment of the committee, a consultative body to give proposals to the People's Bank of China, the central bank, in setting monetary policy, was a result of the central bank law passed in 1995, a central bank official said.
"The regulations are part of clauses of the People's Bank of China Law," the official said by telephone. "This are more detailed rules."
The detailed regulations, published by the official Xinhua news agency, said the governor of the central bank would be named as the chairman of the policy committee.

Members would include senior officials of the People's Bank of China, State Planning Commission, State Economic and Trade Commission, the Ministry of Finance and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange and the China Securities Regulatory Commission, it said.

The central bank would send proposals from the committee together with its annual plans for money supply, interest rates and foreign exchange rates to the State Council, or cabinet, for approval, it said.
Committee members would be removed from their posts and could face criminal charges if found guilty of leaking state and commercial secrets, it said.
